Herb-Crusted Roasted Pork Loin

Served at: Winter Solstice (Yule)

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 1 hour 15 min

This succulent Herb-Crusted Roasted Pork Loin is a centerpiece for any Yule feast, symbolizing abundance and warmth during the longest night of the year. It's a hearty dish meant to be shared, bringing comfort and celebration as families gather to welcome the returning sun.

Ingredients

  • 2-3 pounds (900g-1.4kg) boneless pork loin roast
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves, finely chopped
  • 1 teaspoon dried sage
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) chicken or vegetable broth (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Pat the pork loin roast dry thoroughly with paper towels; this helps create a nice crust.
  3. In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, dried sage, salt, and black pepper.
  4. Rub the herb mixture all over the pork loin, ensuring it's evenly coated.
  5. Place the pork loin in a roasting pan, fat-side up if applicable.
  6. Roast for 60-75 minutes, or until an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C) is reached in the thickest part of the roast.
  7. If desired, pour the broth into the bottom of the roasting pan during the last 15 minutes of cooking to create flavorful pan drippings.
  8. Once cooked, remove the pork loin from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent loosely with foil.
  9. Let the roast rest for at least 10-15 minutes before slicing; this allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a tender and moist result.
  10. Slice the pork loin into thick medallions and serve immediately with any pan drippings.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, sear the pork loin in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side before roasting.
  • Roast root vegetables like carrots, potatoes, and parsnips alongside the pork by adding them to the roasting pan during the last 45 minutes of cooking.
  • A simple pan sauce can be made by deglazing the roasting pan with a splash of white wine or more broth after removing the pork, scraping up any browned bits, and simmering until slightly reduced.
